# xshield_enforcement_status (Data Source)

Reports whether an account and region have converged on the policy Xshield expects, what the next enforcement run would change, and what the cloud connector observes that differs from what was applied.

It reads only, so it can run inside a `check` block. Where checks are evaluated on a schedule, such as HCP Terraform continuous validation, that alerts on drift and stalled pipelines without anyone running an apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Two of the problems examples/enforcement-snapshot/monitor reports, each as a named check with the monitor's
# own condition. The monitor is the full version: every problem, including policy that has never been applied,
# a list of what is waiting, each limit as a variable, and a fail_on list that stops a plan.
data "xshield_enforcement_status" "this" {
  cloud_account_id = "123456789012"
  region           = "us-east-1"
}

locals {
  status        = data.xshield_enforcement_status.this
  where         = "${local.status.cloud_account_id}/${local.status.region}"
  max_apply_age = "24h"

  drift_high = [
    for f in local.status.drift_findings : "  ${f.kind} ${coalesce(f.resource_name, f.resource)}: ${f.detail} (fixed by: ${f.restoration})" if f.severity == "high"
  ]

  # coalesce keeps a null time out of timeadd while nothing is pending.
  apply_overdue = local.status.state == "pending" && timecmp(timeadd(coalesce(local.status.pending_since, plantimestamp()), local.max_apply_age), plantimestamp()) < 0
}

check "xshield_drift_high" {
  assert {
    condition     = length(local.drift_high) == 0
    error_message = join("\n", concat(["Xshield sees high-severity drift in ${local.where}:"], local.drift_high))
  }
}

check "xshield_apply_overdue" {
  assert {
    condition = !local.apply_overdue
    error_message = join("\n", [
      "Approved Xshield policy for ${local.where} has waited more than ${local.max_apply_age} for an enforcement run:",
      "  waiting since ${coalesce(local.status.pending_since, "an unknown time")}: ${length(local.status.pending_security_groups_added)} group(s) to create, ${length(local.status.pending_rules_added)} rule(s) to add, ${length(local.status.pending_rules_removed)} rule(s) to remove, ${length(local.status.pending_attachments_added)} attachment(s) to add. Run the enforcement workspace to apply them.",
    ])
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cloud_account_id` (String) Cloud account to report on.
- `region` (String) Region to report on.

### Optional

- `cloud` (String) Cloud to report on. Only `aws` is supported, and it is the default.

### Read-Only

- `applied_at` (String) When the latest receipt was recorded.
- `applied_attachments` (Map of String) From the last receipt: the attachment import ID, `<network interface ID>_<security group ID>` of each resource the enforcement module created, keyed as the module keys `aws_network_interface_sg_attachment.this`. Empty before the first receipt.
- `applied_rules` (Map of String) From the last receipt: the security group rule ID of each resource the enforcement module created, keyed as the module keys `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.this`, for a key with `/in/`, or `aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule.this`, for a key with `/out/`. Empty before the first receipt.
- `applied_security_groups` (Map of String) From the last receipt: the security group ID of each resource the enforcement module created, keyed as the module keys `aws_security_group.this`. Empty before the first receipt.
- `applied_version` (String) Version in the latest apply receipt. Null when nothing has been applied.
- `drift_evaluated` (Boolean) Whether drift could be evaluated: it needs an applied receipt and a cloud connector observation taken after it. An observation older than the latest apply describes resources that apply replaced, so it is not evaluated.
- `drift_findings` (List of Object) Differences between the cloud as observed and the snapshot as applied. `kind`: what differs, such as `ruleMissing`, `ruleUnmanaged` or `memberUnattached`. `severity`: `high` where access may be wider than approved or a workload is unenforced, otherwise `medium`. `restoration`: `pipeline` when the next enforcement apply restores it, `manual` when Terraform cannot see it and it must be removed by hand, `workload` when the owning workspace's attachment must change. A rule added to an Xshield group outside Terraform is `pipeline` when the latest receipt set `exclusive_rules`, otherwise `manual`. `resource`: AWS ID of the affected resource, or the Xshield asset ID for an attachment finding. `resource_name`: for an attachment finding, the workload as AWS names it, its instance ID or its handle. `key`: snapshot key involved, when there is one. `detail`: human-readable explanation. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--drift_findings))
- `drift_observed_at` (String) When the cloud connector's latest observation was taken.
- `expected_version` (String) Version Xshield expects to be enforced, the hash of everything it asks for.
- `handover_attachments` (Map of String) Before the first receipt of an account moved from connector delivery: the attachment import ID, `<network interface ID>_<security group ID>` of each resource the cloud connector created that the expected snapshot names, keyed as the module keys `aws_network_interface_sg_attachment.this`, so the enforcement workspace imports it rather than creating it again. Empty otherwise.
- `handover_rules` (Map of String) Before the first receipt of an account moved from connector delivery: the security group rule ID of each resource the cloud connector created that the expected snapshot names, keyed as the module keys `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.this`, for a key with `/in/`, or `aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule.this`, for a key with `/out/`, so the enforcement workspace imports it rather than creating it again. Empty otherwise.
- `handover_security_groups` (Map of String) Before the first receipt of an account moved from connector delivery: the security group ID of each resource the cloud connector created that the expected snapshot names, keyed as the module keys `aws_security_group.this`, so the enforcement workspace imports it rather than creating it again. Empty otherwise.
- `last_checked_at` (String) When an enforcement plan last resolved the expected version. A stale value means the pipeline has stopped running, whatever the convergence state says.
- `notices` (List of Object) What Xshield could not enforce in the latest version, and why. A refusal leaves a workload as it was: one that carries an Xshield group keeps it, with the rules last applied, and one that carries none gets none until the cause is fixed. A contained workload's group stays off its interfaces until the containment is reverted. A `groupRefused` group that fits once changed, but not while it changes, is the one exception: the rules its change removes and no new rule replaces come out first, and its new rules go in at the next apply if they then fit. A `portNotNarrowed` notice is about a port still deployed in Xshield on a workload whose customer security group a reverted Full control change no longer narrows: the group again allows more than the port's policy, until the port is deployed again and its change approved, or undeployed. `code`: `assetRefused`, `assetContained`, `groupRefused`, `withdrawing`, `asgPolicyDiffers`, `changeSetHeld` or `portNotNarrowed`. `reason`: the cloud connector's refusal code, as the Xshield portal shows it, such as `NO_FREE_SLOT` or `RULE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED:inbound/ipv4=61`, or for `changeSetHeld` and `portNotNarrowed` the change set's ID. `asset_id`: the Xshield asset the notice is about, when there is one. `group`: the group the notice is about, when there is one: a security group by its key in the snapshot's `security_groups`, one of your own security groups as `<VPC ID>/<name>` for `changeSetHeld` and `portNotNarrowed`, or for `asgPolicyDiffers` the Auto Scaling group by its handle. `asset_name`: the asset as AWS names it, its instance ID or its handle, such as `rds/orders-db`. `since`: for `changeSetHeld`, when the change was approved or, once its revert is requested, when that was; for `portNotNarrowed`, when the revert was requested; null for every other code. `message`: what happened and what it means for the workload. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--notices))
- `pending_attachments_added` (List of String) Keys of interface attachments the next enforcement run will create.
- `pending_rules_added` (List of String) Keys of rules the next enforcement run will add.
- `pending_rules_removed` (List of String) Keys of rules the next enforcement run will remove.
- `pending_security_groups_added` (List of String) Keys of security groups the next enforcement run will create.
- `pending_since` (String) When the oldest policy change not yet applied was published.
- `published` (Boolean) False while Xshield has published nothing for this account and region. `state` is then `unpublished`, versions are null and every list is empty, so checks stay quiet.
- `state` (String) `converged` when the latest receipt matches the expected snapshot, `waiting` when it does but a Full control change still waits on another workspace's apply or on discovery, which its `changeSetHeld` notices name, `pending` when Xshield expects newer policy than was applied, `unapplied` when nothing has been applied yet, `unpublished` when Xshield has published nothing to apply, `handedOver` when the account moved to connector delivery, and the cloud connector keeps the groups the pipeline created.
